Diego — I've reviewed the Synapse markup and the attached order form. High-level legal notes below; detailed comments are in the attached Redwood_MSA_Response_annotated.pdf.

Top items I expect Synapse to want to adjust:
- Term/termination: 24mo term is OK commercially, but we need to preserve our standard early-termination recovery for unused committed capacity. Recommend we add a 90-day notice carve-out for planned migrations (helps Synapse but limits abrupt reductions).
- SLA & credits: their markup narrows our definition of "unavailable" and expands credit triggers to include KV cache misses. We can't accept credits for cache misses — propose clarifying that credits apply to service outages impacting request/response latency only; cache and cache eviction policies are operational controls.
- Data retention & privacy: Synapse added a clause restricting transient KV cache to <7 days. We can agree to a 14-day default with an ops note that some model caches are ephemeral; require exact workload mapping in the order form.
- Indemnity & liability cap: they attempt to carve out third-party claims broadly. We should push for reciprocal indemnities and keep liability cap at the agreed dollars in the order form.

I do have one escalation that will need Commercial sign-off: Synapse asked for a customer-specific SLA credit multiplier for multi-region failover; that's a material SLA variance. If Marissa is comfortable with a capped credit (example: 10% of monthly invoice up to 2 months), I can draft language.

I attached the annotated response. My timeline: I can finalize language for our counsel and share a redline back to Alyssa by EOD Aug 6 if we lock the commercial cap. Otherwise, pushing to Aug 9.

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_Response_annotated.pdf

Thanks,
